title: EVERY CHANGE SHOULD BE REVERSIBLE
script:
Giving an AI write access without version history is like letting someone renovate your house with no before photos.

Every change should leave a trail.

Save a checkpoint before the work starts.

Show exactly what changed.

Let the agent test the result.

And if the new version is worse, roll back instead of patching over the mistake.

Good automation doesn’t just move fast.

It makes every step reversible.
audience: People using AI coding agents, automation tools and assistants.
concept: The Reversible Rowhouse Folio: a large, irregular paper rowhouse is altered through a slotted roof mechanism. An unsafe overwrite nearly loses the original roof, so a paper-gold history spine catches it. The Bot then stores the intact house as a keyed checkpoint, installs a visibly different coral roof, performs a physical rain test, observes a leak and sagging floor, and pulls the checkpoint mechanism to restore the original roof and dry interior. A successful repeat test and reverse-folding history trail prove that the whole path—not merely the final object—is reversible.
rationale: One persistent tactile hero turns version history into physical evidence. The opening establishes a readable original state and the danger of untracked change; the middle shows checkpointing, comparison and a consequential test; the ending restores the exact opening silhouette and successfully retests it. The rowhouse, roof profiles, water path and sagging floor remain legible without captions at 360×640. All motion is bounded to explicit paper parts, affine transforms, keyed contacts and timed frame events; the single production-specific SVG contains the complete prop system and environmental cues.

shots.narration: Giving an AI write access without version history is like letting someone renovate your house with no before photos.
physical_sequence: Establish the intact rowhouse folio from x82–646 and y300–974: a tall cream façade, offset teal pitched roof, three uneven windows and a flat dry floor strip.
Bot at x132,y824 turns the charcoal write latch, grips the teal roof at its exposed eave anchor and lifts it from two keyed slots.
A black discard mouth opens behind the roofline; the original roof starts descending while a broad coral replacement roof approaches from the right.
Bot notices the original roof is about to disappear and arrests the replacement just short of contact, leaving the unsafe overwrite visibly unresolved.
shots.consequence: The original configuration is visibly being lost while the proposed renovation is poised to occupy its anchors.

quality.purpose: Make unversioned write access feel physically dangerous before introducing the safe mechanism.
quality.hero: The intact-to-threatened Reversible Rowhouse Folio and its mutually exclusive roof panels.
quality.primary_action: Bot unlocks and removes the original roof while an untracked replacement advances.
quality.before: The teal pitched roof is seated in both façade slots and the cream interior is dry and level.
quality.after: The teal roof hangs above the discard mouth, the slots are empty and the coral roof is stopped just before insertion.
secondary_motion: Bot’s antenna leans toward the falling roof during the late realization.
The lifted roof’s lower paper edge lags by four frames after the grip stops.
The discard mouth opens only far enough to expose the loss path, then holds under tension.
environment: Warm-cream tabletop with an irregular deckled front edge at y1000
Charcoal pinboard seam behind the roof at y286
Paper-gold archive rail fixed along the left side of the folio
quality.exit_overlap: A paper-gold catch tongue begins extending from the archive rail before the roof can drop.

energy.dominant_action: The original roof is physically extracted and begins falling toward irreversible loss.
energy.character_response: Bot shifts from focused leverage to a wide, off-balance surprised arrest.
energy.local_reaction: Only the lifted roof, approaching replacement and façade respond around the empty roof slots.
energy.residual_motion: The roof edge and Bot antenna settle after the abrupt stop.
energy.next_action_overlap: The gold catch tongue enters beneath the falling roof.

shots.narration: Every change should leave a trail.
physical_sequence: Continue the falling motion in a closer view without Bot.
The paper-gold catch tongue slides under the teal roof and hooks its eave notch before the discard mouth can take it.
A narrow accordion history strip unfolds from the left rail; its first keyed bay receives the teal roof while its second bay holds the waiting coral roof.
The discard mouth closes, leaving both ordered roof states physically connected to the house by the gold strip.
shots.consequence: The formerly vanishing original becomes the first retained state in a visible, ordered trail.

shots.narration: Save a checkpoint before the work starts.
physical_sequence: The teal roof returns to both façade slots, restoring the complete dry opening state before the renovation resumes.
Bot braces the folio and pulls the paper-gold checkpoint tab from the left archive rail.
A full-height gold silhouette plate travels behind the house; keyed apertures align with the roof, windows and level floor strip.
The plate slides back into the archive pocket carrying a compact raised relief of the intact configuration, while the live house remains unchanged.
shots.consequence: A complete original configuration is stored before any replacement part touches the house.

quality.purpose: Show checkpointing as a concrete precondition that preserves the whole starting configuration.
quality.hero: The intact rowhouse and its matching gold silhouette checkpoint plate.
quality.primary_action: Bot pulls a keyed plate behind the untouched house and archives its complete original configuration.
quality.before: The house has been restored but no complete checkpoint plate is stored in the archive pocket.
quality.after: The live house remains intact and dry while a matching gold relief is visibly parked in the archive rail.
secondary_motion: Bot leans away from the rail during the pull, keeping its grip aligned to the checkpoint tab anchor.
The raised checkpoint relief appears from bottom to top as the plate passes behind each keyed feature.
The gold tab gives a small seated bounce when the archived plate reaches its stop.

energy.dominant_action: A full-house checkpoint plate is physically aligned, imprinted and stored before alteration.
energy.character_response: Bot braces low, pulls with focused effort and releases tension when the plate seats.
energy.local_reaction: The tab, checkpoint plate and supported façade respond locally at the archive rail.
energy.residual_motion: The foil tab and Bot antenna settle after the pocket stop.
energy.next_action_overlap: Bot begins turning toward the proposed coral roof.

physical_sequence: Without Bot, the teal roof lifts from the live house and folds left on the attached history strip while the archived checkpoint remains visible behind it.

Both roof baselines align across the hinge, making the lost pitch, added flat deck and open drainage notch visually exact.
shots.consequence: The changed geometry is isolated by direct physical alignment between preserved before-state and live after-state.

quality.after: The checkpoint leaf shows the teal pitched roof while the aligned live leaf shows the coral flat roof and its drainage notch.

shots.narration: Let the agent test the result.
physical_sequence: The folio closes to the live coral-roof house; Bot grips the exposed rain-ribbon anchor above the roof.
Bot pulls the translucent teal ribbon downward at constant speed, carrying three large droplet cutouts across the coral roof profile.
The first two droplets pool behind the flat roof lip; the third follows the open notch and enters the upper window.
On contact, the cream floor strip turns teal from left to right and sags fourteen pixels at its unsupported center.
shots.consequence: The test produces visible evidence that the new roof leaks and damages the interior floor.

quality.purpose: Show the agent performing an actual repeatable test whose result changes the physical hero.
quality.hero: The coral-roof house under a descending paper rain ribbon.
quality.primary_action: Bot pulls the rain ribbon; water follows the replacement roof’s notch and deforms the interior floor.
quality.before: The coral roof is installed, the translucent rain ribbon is raised and the interior floor is cream, level and dry.
quality.after: Droplets are pooled and leaking through the notch; the floor is teal-stained and visibly sagging.
secondary_motion: Bot’s pulling arm stays resolved to the ribbon anchor while its torso leans back and antenna tips toward the leak.
The pooled droplet cutouts compress slightly against the coral roof lip before the leak releases.
The floor’s paper fibers lag behind the central sag and stop without global shake.
environment: Warm-cream tabletop catching the house’s lower-right shadow
Charcoal pinboard seam supporting the rain-ribbon guide
Paper-gold archive rail remaining visibly closed at frame left
quality.exit_overlap: Bot releases the rain ribbon with one hand while reaching for the gold checkpoint tab with the other.

energy.dominant_action: The controlled rain ribbon exposes a leak that stains and deforms the interior floor.
energy.character_response: Bot changes from focused pulling to worried forward attention at the first interior contact.
energy.local_reaction: Only the window flap, floor strip and contacted coral roof answer the water path.
energy.residual_motion: The wet floor and released ribbon continue a brief material settle.
energy.next_action_overlap: Bot’s free hand closes on the checkpoint tab before the sag fully settles.

shots.narration: And if the new version is worse, roll back instead of patching over the mistake.
physical_sequence: Bot plants both feet and pulls the paper-gold checkpoint tab through its full marked travel, without touching the leak or adding any patch.
The linked checkpoint carriage withdraws the coral roof into the right history bay while the teal original roof travels from the archive rail toward the empty façade slots.
At the carriage midpoint, the wet floor strip rotates once around its concealed paper hinge, presenting its preserved cream dry face.
The teal roof lands in both keyed slots; the gold checkpoint relief aligns behind the façade and the house returns to its exact opening silhouette.
shots.consequence: The failed configuration is retained in history while every damaged live component is restored from the checkpoint.

quality.purpose: Demonstrate genuine restoration of the preserved state rather than cosmetic repair of the failed version.
quality.hero: The linked checkpoint carriage exchanging roof states and reversing the wet floor.
quality.primary_action: Bot pulls one checkpoint tab that removes the failed roof, reinstates the original roof and restores the dry floor.
quality.before: The coral roof leaks, the interior floor is teal and sagging, and the original roof remains in the archive trail.
quality.after: The coral roof is retained in its history bay, the teal roof is locked into the house and the floor is cream, dry and level.
secondary_motion: Bot’s shoulders rise under load while both grips remain resolved to the gold tab anchor.
The two roofs pass on separate shallow depth rails so their silhouettes never intersect ambiguously.
The restored roof compresses into its slots, rebounds two pixels and carries a short paper-edge lag.

energy.local_reaction: The two roofs, floor strip and checkpoint tab respond in a bounded sequence around the carriage path.
energy.residual_motion: The restored teal eave, dry floor and Bot antenna settle after the carriage stop.
energy.next_action_overlap: The rain ribbon rewinds for a repeat test before the gold tab has completely stopped vibrating.

shots.narration: Good automation doesn’t just move fast.
physical_sequence: With Bot absent, the same translucent rain ribbon descends at the same measured speed and alignment used for the failed test.
All three droplet cutouts meet the restored teal pitch and travel outward along its overlapping shingle edge.
The droplets enter the side gutter and slide into a gold catch cup outside the façade.
The interior floor remains cream and level throughout the complete test window.
shots.consequence: The restored version passes the same real test; speed is secondary to the dry, unchanged interior.

quality.purpose: Prove the rollback recovered working behavior under the identical test conditions.
quality.hero: The restored teal-roof rowhouse shedding repeat-test water safely into its gutter.
quality.primary_action: The repeated rain ribbon follows the restored roof into the exterior catch cup without entering the house.
quality.before: The original teal roof and dry floor are restored; the repeat rain ribbon is raised.
quality.after: All test droplets sit in the exterior catch cup and the interior floor remains flat, cream and dry.
secondary_motion: Droplets accelerate along the pitch, then decelerate visibly in the gutter bend.
The catch cup dips four pixels under the third droplet and returns.
The dry floor remains deliberately still as the control evidence.

physical_sequence: The attached gold history spine fans across the frame, displaying three large physical states in order: intact checkpoint, coral-roof test failure and restored dry house.
A gold return tab reverses direction; the wet-test state folds onto the failed roof state, then both fold backward into the checkpoint bay.
The failed coral roof remains preserved inside the closed history pocket while the live teal roof, windows and dry floor align exactly with the opening composition.
The gold spine seats beneath the house as a visible retained edge, leaving the restored rowhouse upright and the exterior test droplets safely held in their cup.
shots.consequence: The entire demonstrated path can run backward to the exact starting state without erasing the attempted change or its test evidence.

quality.purpose: Pay off reversibility by visibly traversing the recorded steps backward and matching the opening state.

art_direction.intentional_irregularity: The fan uses unequal leaf angles and preserves every hand-cut asymmetry, allowing the final ridge, bowed wall and uneven windows to match the opening rather than a perfected replacement.

asset_usage.description: Existing canonical Bot used without geometry changes. Registered high-energy-paper performances target only bot; authored arm grips use declared prop anchors and inverse grip resolution.

The single minimum new prop asset: rowhouse façade, teal original roof, coral replacement roof, keyed slots, discard mouth, gold checkpoint plate, archive rail, accordion history spine, hinged two-state floor, rain ribbon, droplets, gutter, catch cup and the three physical environment cues. Requires agent-assisted source construction, anchor metadata and asset review; remains production-specific with no canonical promotion.

development_scope: Measure the supplied narration at voice_speed 1.08 and derive shot boundaries from the eight consecutive exact narration substrings; target the natural approximately 30–40 second delivery rather than imposing fixed visual durations.
Create one bounded production-specific SVG and matching metadata with named geometry for every reaction target and contact anchor; preserve the reused Bot’s canonical geometry.

Implement the eight declared rowhouse action bindings as finite GSAP frame events using affine transforms, keyed slot contacts, shallow depth rails and the two-faced floor hinge; no physics simulation or unregistered selector is required.
Author and verify inverse grip resolution for the write latch, rain-ribbon anchor and checkpoint tab after primary and reaction transforms.

Keep primary action within y280–990 on the 720×1280 authoring canvas and reserve y1090–1180 for captions; verify the roof profiles, water path, floor state and rollback at native 360×640 without captions.
Limit each declared reaction radius to its named real parts and preserve the specified small amplitudes, falloff and delays; unsupported parts remain still.

Submit moving roughs with and without captions to both independent direction critics before final artwork, including ordered native frames around each contact, landing, hinge seat and water impact plus motion traces with their sampling limitations.
After rough approval, complete production-specific asset review, final moving QA, audio finishing and a human watch-and-approve pass; do not publish or treat successful encoding as approval.
